title: Safety-Critical Aerospace Software
subtitle: DO-178B/C × Embedded Control × Verification × Certification × Technical Leadership
description: A rigorous learning route for safety-critical airborne embedded software, from lifecycle assurance and requirements through target verification, structural coverage, certification readiness and technical leadership.
methodTitle: Build the assurance argument, challenge the implementation, then defend the evidence
methodSteps: Study the stage concept and identify the lifecycle objectives, data and accountable roles.
Answer foundation questions precisely before working difficult design, target and verification scenarios.
Treat traceability, configuration, verification results and problem reports as connected assurance evidence.
Make management and certification decisions using explicit assumptions, residual gaps and closure ownership.

caseStudy.title: Safety-Critical Engine Control Software
caseStudy.description: A dual-channel airborne engine-control application uses model-based control logic, generated and handwritten embedded code, ARINC 429 and CAN interfaces, target processors, HIL benches and certification evidence under a DO-178B/C programme.

notice: Employer-neutral learning material. The supplied role description establishes coverage only. Licensed standards, approved programme plans and certification-authority guidance remain authoritative.
matrixTitle: Aerospace Software Lifecycle and Evidence Matrix
matrix: Planning and assurance
Define lifecycle, standards, responsibilities, reviews and evidence strategy
Programme, quality, certification, suppliers
Defend why the planned lifecycle and independence are adequate for the software level and programme context.
Requirements
Develop high-level requirements and manage derived requirements
System safety, control engineering, verification
Maintain bidirectional traceability and justify every derived behaviour and assumption.
Architecture and design
Define software architecture, interfaces, low-level design and control partitioning
Hardware, models, generated code, communications
Show that design decisions are complete, verifiable and consistent with resource and safety constraints.
Model-based development
Control models, code generation, model verification and tool use
MATLAB/Simulink/Stateflow, compiler, target
Separate model intent, generated implementation and verification evidence without assuming automation proves correctness.
Implementation
Develop and troubleshoot C/C++/assembly software on target processors
BSP, compiler, linker, memory, timing
Explain target-specific behaviour, resource constraints and low-level failure mechanisms.
Communications and control
Integrate ARINC 429, CAN, Ethernet, engine-control and diagnostic behaviour
Sensors, actuators, networks, test benches
Reason about data validity, latency, failure containment and control authority end to end.
Verification and HIL
Review, analyse, test and independently verify software requirements and design
Host tools, target hardware, benches, coverage
Construct a verification strategy that demonstrates requirements satisfaction and detects unintended behaviour.
Coverage and problem closure
Analyse structural coverage, close gaps and control problem reports
Tests, code, traceability, change control
Distinguish missing tests, dead code, deactivated code and unintended functionality, then drive justified closure.
Configuration and certification
Control baselines, changes, audits, certification data and SOI readiness
CM, QA, programme, customer, authority
Demonstrate reproducibility, objective evidence and closure of lifecycle findings.
Technical leadership
Plan, estimate, track, report, mentor and lead corrective action
Global teams, management, customers, quality
Lead a small technical organisation without weakening engineering independence or evidence quality.

architectureExercise.title: 30-minute airborne engine-control assurance exercise
architectureExercise.prompt: Design and defend the software lifecycle and evidence strategy for a safety-critical engine-control change involving a Stateflow control update, generated C code, ARINC 429 input, CAN diagnostics and HIL verification.
structure: Clarify the system requirement, software level, safety assumptions and affected baselines.
Decompose the change into high-level requirements, derived requirements, architecture and low-level design.
Explain model, generated-code, handwritten-code and tool responsibilities.
Define reviews, analysis, host tests, target tests, HIL tests and structural-coverage closure.
Describe configuration identification, change control, problem reporting and reproducible build evidence.
Prepare the certification-data and SOI-readiness argument, including open findings and accountable closure.
challenges: The system requirement omits a sensor-invalid transition discovered during model design.
Generated code introduces defensive branches not exercised by normal requirements-based tests.
A compiler update changes object code and invalidates part of the existing verification evidence.
The HIL bench cannot reproduce a rare ARINC 429 timing fault observed on aircraft hardware.
A high-severity problem report remains open near a certification review.
Programme schedule pressure conflicts with verification independence and audit closure.

days.title: Lifecycle Assurance and Planning
days.focus: DO-178B/C context, software levels, lifecycle plans, standards, independence, estimation and evidence strategy.
days.deliverable: Create a software lifecycle and assurance-plan map for an engine-control change.

days.title: Requirements, Derived Behaviour and Traceability
days.focus: System decomposition, high-level requirements, derived requirements, rationale, traceability and review quality.
days.deliverable: Build a traceability chain from customer need to software requirement and verification case.

days.title: Software Architecture and Low-Level Design
days.focus: Architecture, interfaces, control/data flow, low-level design, resource constraints and design reviews.
days.deliverable: Produce an architecture and design review package for a control-law component.

days.title: Model-Based Development and Code Generation
days.focus: MATLAB/Simulink/Stateflow models, generated code, model verification, tool use and model-code consistency.
days.deliverable: Define the assurance boundary and verification plan for a generated control component.

days.title: Embedded Implementation and Target Debugging
days.focus: C/C++, assembly, Python support tools, compiler/linker behaviour, memory, timing and target troubleshooting.
days.deliverable: Diagnose a target-only failure and document the evidence needed for closure.

days.title: Avionics Communications, Engine Control and Diagnostics
days.focus: ARINC 429, CAN, Ethernet, control loops, data validity, diagnostics and failure handling.
days.deliverable: Trace a sensor-to-actuator and diagnostic path with timing and validity constraints.

days.title: Verification Strategy and HIL
days.focus: Reviews, analysis, requirements-based testing, robustness, independence, target testing and HIL benches.
days.deliverable: Create a multi-level verification strategy and HIL test architecture.

days.title: Structural Coverage and Problem Closure
days.focus: Coverage analysis, gap classification, additional verification, dead/deactivated code and problem reports.
days.deliverable: Close a structural-coverage gap with traceable technical rationale.

days.title: Configuration, Quality, Certification and SOI
days.focus: Configuration/change management, baselines, audits, certification data, findings and SOI readiness.
days.deliverable: Prepare an auditable release baseline and SOI evidence index.

days.title: Programme Metrics, CAPA and Technical Leadership
days.focus: Planning, tracking, status reviews, root cause, corrective/preventive action, mentoring and global-team leadership.
days.deliverable: Lead an evidence-based recovery plan for a late safety-critical software release.

quiz.q: A behaviour is introduced during software design but has no direct parent system requirement. What is the first assurance concern?
options: It must be hidden in low-level design
It must be identified, justified, traced and communicated as a derived requirement
It needs only a code comment
It can wait until structural coverage
quiz.why: Derived behaviour must be visible to the appropriate lifecycle and safety stakeholders and must receive requirements and verification control.

quiz.q: Why is structural coverage analysis not a substitute for requirements-based testing?
options: Coverage measures execution structure, not whether requirements are complete and correctly satisfied
Requirements testing is optional on target
Coverage automatically proves absence of defects
quiz.why: Structural coverage reveals code exercised or not exercised; the primary verification argument still begins with requirements and expected behaviour.

quiz.q: What is the strongest response to an unresolved high-severity problem report near certification review?
options: Assess impact, define disposition and closure authority, and make the residual gap explicit in readiness status
quiz.why: Certification readiness depends on transparent problem status, technical impact and controlled disposition.
